title: Hodge Theory and Complex Algebraic Geometry I & II

definitions.statement: J^k(X) = H^(2k-1)(X, C) / (F^k H^(2k-1)(X, C) + H^(2k-1)(X, Z)), complex torus parameterizing homologically trivial cycles.
AJ_k: CH^k(X)_hom -> J^k(X) sending cycle sum n_i Z_i to integral of holomorphic forms over chains.
Conjectural filtration F^* on Chow groups CH^k(X)_Q reflecting Hodge coniveau.

theorems.label: Lefschetz Hard Theorem & Primitive Decomposition
theorems.statement: H^k(X, Q) decomposes into primitive cohomology P^(p,q) under Lefschetz operator L.

theorems.label: Voisin's Counterexample to Variational Generalized Hodge
theorems.statement: The generalized Hodge conjecture for variations of Hodge structures fails in codimension >= 2.

theorems.label: Bloch's Conjecture for Surfaces with p_g = 0
theorems.statement: CH_0(S)_hom = 0 for surfaces with geometric genus p_g = 0 under group actions.

conjectures.label: Generalized Hodge Conjecture (Grothendieck)
conjectures.statement: The largest sub-Hodge structure of H^k(X, Q) contained in F^p H^k(X, C) comes from an algebraic subvariety of codimension p.

open_gaps: Mumford's theorem (1968) proves Chow groups CH_0(X) can be infinite-dimensional, creating obstruction to geometric representation.
computational_handles: Gröbner basis computation for ideals of algebraic subvarieties representing Hodge classes.
Primitive cohomology decomposition on Fermat hypersurfaces.
Abel-Jacobi regulator evaluation for cycles on Calabi-Yau threefolds.

citations.ref: Voisin, C. (2002). Hodge Theory and Complex Algebraic Geometry, I & II, Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics, 76 & 77.
